record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: If every node in the network is restricted to sending only linear transformations of its incoming messages, can one prove or disprove the network coding conjecture under that restriction?

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Prove or disprove the network coding conjecture when all nodes are restricted to sending linear transformations of their incoming messages.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite directed acyclic graph with edge capacities, together with a set of $k$ source–sink pairs $(s_1, t_1), \ldots, (s_k, t_k)$. Each source $s_i$ holds an independent message $X_i$ taking values in a finite alphabet (identified with a vector space over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$), and the goal is for sink $t_i$ to recover $X_i$ exactly. A network code assigns to every edge $e = (u,v)$ a function whose output (sent along $e$) is computed from the symbols received by $u$ on its incoming edges (and, if $u = s_i$, from $X_i$); each sink $t_j$ applies a decoding function to its incoming symbols. The routing rate of an instance is the maximum throughput achievable when every internal node may only forward (copy) symbols received on incoming edges, while the network coding rate is the maximum throughput achievable when arbitrary functions are allowed at internal nodes.

The network coding conjecture asserts that for every multiple-unicast instance on a directed acyclic graph, the network coding rate equals the routing rate (equivalently, coding offers no throughput advantage over routing for multiple unicast).

A network code is called linear if for every edge $e = (u,v)$, the symbol transmitted on $e$ is an $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear transformation of the vector of symbols available at $u$ (its incoming symbols, together with its source message if $u$ is a source), and every sink's decoder is also $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear.

Problem: Either prove or disprove the network coding conjecture under the restriction that every node is allowed to send only linear transformations of its incoming messages. That is, decide whether, for every multiple-unicast instance, the maximum rate achievable by a linear network code equals the routing rate.
artifact.status_search_result: The network coding conjecture (no coding advantage over routing for multiple unicast in DAGs) is a well-known open problem; even its restriction to linear network codes remains unresolved. Partial progress exists (e.g., results by Langberg–Medard and others bounding the gap and connections to I/O complexity and pebbling), but no proof or disproof of the linear case has been published.

status_evidence.title: On the Multiple Unicast Network Coding Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the multiple unicast conjecture and partial progress, indicating the conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The multiple-unicast network coding conjecture remains open, including restricted variants.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds for Multiplication via Network Coding
status_evidence.snippet: Uses the network coding conjecture (still unresolved) and its linear version as a hypothesis for circuit lower bounds.
status_evidence.claim: The linear network coding conjecture is invoked as an unproven hypothesis.
